THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE  COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2023:KHC:33784  CRL.P No. 2525 of 2022  ORDER
The petitioner-accused No.3 is sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 504, 506, 448, 385 r/w 34 of IPC.

2 . The case of the prosecution is that, initially the FIR was registered against accused Nos.1 and 2 alleging that, they induced respondent No.2 to invest the money for establishing a saree shop and after collecting the money have not established the saree shop.

In the further statement respondent No.2 as stated that, accused No.3 herein instigated the accused Nos.1 and 2 to lodge the FIR in Crime No.54/2020, alleging that the respondent No.2 after lending the money used to charge exorbitant interest on the money lent.

Thereafter, the accused No.3 barged into the Mobile shop of the brother of the respondent No.2 and threatened them with dire consequences demanding that he shall not ask the accused No.1 to return the money.
3. The cognizance taken of the aforesaid offences is impugned in this petition.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the allegations made in the FIR, even accepting on the face of it, does not satisfy the essential elements to constitute the commission of the offence of extortion.

He further submits that, threatening with dire consequences has not caused the breach of public peace or commission of any other offences to constitute the commission of offence under section 506 of IPC.
Hence, the continuation of the criminal proceedings against the petitioners will be an abuse of process of law.
5. Respondent No.2 though served with notice has not chosen to appear in person or through her counsel.

6. On the other hand, learned HCGP for the State submits that the allegation made against the accused No.3 constitute the commission of cognizable offence, and the veracity of the allegations can be considered at the time of the Trial, and at this stage, the same cannot be gone into.

sentences.text: Considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.
In the FIR there is no allegation that this accused trespassed into the Mobile shop belonging to the brother of the respondent No.2.

However, in the further statement which was recorded on 22.9.2020, the defacto-complainant alleged that accused No.3 barged into the Mobile shop belonging to the brother of the respondent No.2 and threatened them with dire consequences demanding that he shall not ask the accused No.1 to return the money.

9. The defacto complainant has not offered any explanation for the delay in making the statement against the accused No.3 which clearly infers that the statement was made so as to falsely implicate the accused No.3, since it is alleged that accused No.3 instigated the accused Nos.1 and 2 to lodge the FIR for the offence of cheating and charging exorbitant interest against the defacto-complainant.
10. The accused Nos.1 and 2 had filed the FIR which was registered in Crime No.171/2020 for the offence of cheating against the defacto complainant.
Thereafter, the respondent No.2 as a counter blast lodged the FIR registered in Crime No.54/2020 for the offence of cheating.
To constitute the offence under Section 385 of IPC, a person must have committed extortion by putting any person in fear of death or of grievous hurt to that person or to any other.

12. In the instant case, the allegation that, the accused No.3 instigated the accused Nos.1 and 2 to lodge the FIR for the offence of cheating and charging exorbitant interest does not fall under the definition of extortion since the respondent No.2 has not delivered any money or property to the accused Nos.1 and 2 in view of the alleged threat given by the accused No.3 herein.

13. The allegation that the accused No.3 threatened the defacto complainant with dire consequences in the event he demanded to return the money from the accused No.1 has not resulted in causing breach of public peace or commission of any other offence by the defacto-complainant, which is an essential element to constitute the commission of offence under Section 504 of IPC.
14.
Hence, the essential elements to constitute the commission of offence alleged against the petitioner-accused NC: 2023:KHC:33784 No.3 are conspicuously absent.
Therefore, the continuation of the criminal proceedings in the absence of the same will be an abuse of process of law.

15. Accordingly I pass the following:
ORDER i) The criminal petition is allowed Kiran V N @ Vasu vs State Of Karnataka on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133136686/
